title: Hummus vs. guacamole: nutrition differences

seo.title: Hummus vs. guacamole: calories, protein, fiber and fat
seo.meta_description: Per 100 g, plain hummus: 243 calories, 7.3 g protein and 5.4 g fiber; guacamole: 155 calories, 1.9 g protein and 6.5 g fiber. See a 50 g serving.
seo.search_intent: Compare hummus and guacamole for calories, protein, fiber and fat

excerpt: Hummus and guacamole are both plant-based dips, but they are not nutritionally interchangeable. Per 100 g, the current USDA references used here provide 243 calories and 7.3 g protein for hummus versus 155 calories and 1.9 g for guacamole. Guacamole provides slightly more fiber, 6.5 versus 5.4 g/100 g, and less energy. In a 50 g portion, that is about 122 versus 78 calories.
content_html:
Hummus and guacamole occupy the same slot on a snack table, sandwich or toast, but they get there through very different ingredients. Hummus provides substantially more protein; guacamole is less calorie-dense and slightly higher in fiber by weight in the references compared here.

Compare 100 g, then a 50 g serving

Per 100 gHummusGuacamole
Calories243155
Protein7.3 g1.9 g
Fat17.1 g14.2 g
Fiber5.4 g6.5 g
Carbohydrate14.9 g8.4 g

At 50 g, hummus works out to about 122 calories, 3.7 g protein and 2.7 g fiber. Guacamole provides about 78 calories, 1.0 g protein and 3.3 g fiber.

Hummus: more protein from chickpeas and sesame

The legume base explains much of hummus's protein advantage, while tahini adds some more. Even so, 3.7 g in a 50 g portion is a contribution rather than a large protein serving.

Guacamole: lower energy density in this comparison

Avocado contains fat but also substantial water and fiber. In the survey reference used here, guacamole is 88 calories/100 g lower than hummus. At a 50 g serving, the difference is about 44 calories.

Both contain fat, but recipes matter

Hummus gets fat from tahini, chickpeas and any added oil; guacamole gets most from avocado. Unsaturated fats predominate, but generous added oil or other ingredients can move the numbers.

Salt can overturn a simple comparison

Commercial dips and homemade recipes vary widely in sodium. If sodium is important, compare the actual labels rather than assigning one universal value to hummus or guacamole.

Which should you choose?

Hummus if you want more protein and the chickpea-sesame profile; guacamole if you want slightly more fiber by weight and lower energy density in these preparations. They do not need to be nutritional rivals: each brings a different food matrix, and serving size shapes the practical difference.

faq.question: Which has more protein, hummus or guacamole?
faq.answer: Hummus by a wide margin in these references: 7.3 versus 1.9 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Guacamole here: 155 versus 243 calories/100 g, or about 78 versus 122 calories per 50 g.

faq.question: Which has less fat?
faq.answer: The guacamole reference at 14.2 versus 17.1 g/100 g, although recipes can change this gap.
